props.title: Day of Anger

sections.content: **Day of Anger (1967)** (1967) stands as one of the most intense and psychologically complex Spaghetti Westerns, with Lee Van Cleef delivering a career-defining performance as gunfighter Frank Talby. The film subverts typical mentor-student Western tropes established in films like **The Magnificent Seven** (1960) by showing the dark side of apprenticeship. Director Tonino Valerii, who learned his craft under Sergio Leone on **For a Few Dollars More** (1965), crafts a morally ambiguous tale that explores power corruption and betrayal with striking visual style.

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond its era, establishing themes that would resurface in later revenge-driven Westerns. **Django** (1966) and **The Great Silence** (1968) built on its foundation of moral ambiguity, while modern homages like **Django Unchained** (2012) drew from its master-student dynamic. Van Cleef's portrayal of Talby created a template for complex antagonists that influenced characters in films like **Unforgiven** (1992).

Valerii's direction showcases the best elements of Spaghetti Western style - extreme close-ups, dramatic zooms, and expansive vistas shot in Almería, Spain. The film's technical achievements, particularly Riz Ortolani's score and Marcello Masciocchi's cinematography, influenced later genre entries like **Once Upon a Time in the West** (1968) and **My Name is Nobody** (1973). sections.content: Lee Van Cleef's commanding presence in **Day of Anger** (1967) cemented his status as a Spaghetti Western icon. His portrayal of morally ambiguous characters, perfected in films like **For a Few Dollars More** (1965) and The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966), reached its apex here. The actor's ability to shift between menacing villain and charismatic mentor influenced countless Western performances, including Michael Fassbender's character in **Slow West** (2015).
